memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "The most gentle and sensitive man among you will have no compassion on his own brother or the wife he loves or his surviving children... So gentle and sensitive will a woman be that she would not venture to touch the ground with the sole of her foot... These will be the curses even against the most refined among you during the siege." — Deut 28:54-57 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This continues the horror of the siege, showing how desperation can strip away even the tenderest human affection. The gentlest man, the most refined woman — even these would be hardened by suffering into unthinkable cruelty toward those they loved most. It is a devastating picture of what extreme circumstances, under the weight of judgment, can do to the human heart.

There is a sobering truth here about human nature. We like to think our kindness and love are unshakeable, part of who we are. But this passage warns that apart from God's sustaining grace, even the gentlest heart can grow hard. Our virtue is not as secure as we imagine when we stand on our own.

This should keep us humble. None of us should say, "I could never become cold or cruel." Our tenderness, our compassion, our love — these are gifts sustained by God's grace, not achievements we can take for granted.

And it drives us, once again, to our need for a Saviour and for the transforming work of the Spirit. On our own, our hearts are prone to harden. But God promises to His people a new heart — to remove the heart of stone and give a heart of flesh (Ezek 36:26). Only He can keep our hearts soft. So we lean on Him, asking daily that His grace would preserve in us the tenderness that only He can sustain.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Am I humble about my own capacity for hardness apart from God's grace?
2. Do I depend on God to keep my heart soft and compassionate?
3. Where do I need to ask God for a "heart of flesh" today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, keep my heart soft. I know that apart from Your grace even my tenderness could harden. Give me a heart of flesh, and sustain compassion in me by Your Spirit. Amen.
